title: Characteristic function of a Gaussian linear functional
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous linear functional. For a vector $Z$ with independent standard Gaussian coordinates, the characteristic function of $L(Z)$ is
\[
\mathbb E\bigl[e^{iL(Z)}\bigr]=\exp\!\left(-\frac12\sum_{j=1}^n L(e_j)^2\right),
\]
where $e_j$ are the standard coordinate vectors.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a continuous real-linear functional on $\mathbb R^n$
The measure is the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures
